ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute as no refund due: the sole off-route segment (09:20–09:26) is exempt under RD-5 by the rider's own pre-segment general route authorisation; record the RD-1 review outcome, keep the metered RydeTAXI fare as charged, and do not apply any account action.
ruling.reasoning:
The ride was a metered RydeTAXI trip, so the fare follows the meter rather than the quote: total $45.04 comprises base $3.90, distance $30.46 for 21.60 km, time $9.10 for 35.0 min, waiting $0.11 and platform $1.47, with no surge [F7][F6]. Any refund therefore turns on RD-2, whose non-metered branch does not apply and whose metered branch pays only for unexempt off-route segments [RD-2].

There is a single off-route segment, the 09:20–09:26 loop that drove 4.04 km where the optimal route covers 1.86 km, adding 2.18 km and straying up to 1027 m from the optimal route [F3]; the trip-wide +2.3 km against 19.3 km optimal is that same segment [F1]. RD-1 is engaged: no percentage or absolute threshold exists, and every such segment must be reviewed under RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5 [RD-1].

RD-4 does not excuse it. No traffic incident was recorded near the optimal route in the trip window [F15], and the only congestion record on the optimal route — EAST COAST PARKWAY at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 08:58–09:20 [F12] — is corroborative only and cannot stand alone as an exemption [RD-4]. The driver's post-trip explanation that he "went round" because traffic was building [F11] is a statement, not the traffic evidence RD-4(a) requires [RD-4].

The decisive question is RD-5, the rider's consent, and the trace leaves it to me. The driver asked at 09:17 whether to take another way because of ECP congestion [F8], and the rider replied at 09:18: "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F9], two minutes before the segment started at 09:20 [F3]. The chat record is complete and every message timestamped [F10], so consent is properly evidenced by the rider's own message sent before the segment [RD-5]. Those words are the policy's own example of a general route authorisation — "take whichever way is faster" [RD-5]. A general route choice covers the route chosen to reach the destination, and the alternative that the rider's authorisation selected is consistent with the recorded conditions: the corridor the driver named was slow (ECP band 2, 10–19 km/h) [F12][F8] while the airport corridor was free-flowing (AIRPORT BOULEVARD band 5, 40–49 km/h) [F13]; no incident and fair weather remove any other branch [F15][F16]. The general authorisation does not extend to an errand or loop of the driver's own [RD-5], but nothing in the record places this segment on any such errand — there is no stop, no destination off the route, and no fact showing the loop reached nothing; the only materials tying the segment to a purpose are the congestion exchange [F8][F9] and the traffic record [F12]. The segment is therefore exempt and adds nothing refundable.

Because no unexempt segment remains, the RD-2 amount is Σ(unexempt extra_km) × this trip's per-km rate; the rate is $30.46 ÷ 21.60 km = $1.4102/km and Σ = 0 km, so 0 × $1.4102 = $0.00, and no_action is the outcome under RD-2 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. The metered waiting unit of $0.11 for 0.4 min is chargeable on a RydeTAXI trip and is not refundable [F5][RD-3]. The billed excess of $3.31 for 2.35 km [F4] is not refundable either, since it is the price of the exempt segment and of corridor variation RD-2 does not restore [RD-2].

RD-6's add-on does not arise: the execution trace marks the prior-upheld-route-dispute element ✗, the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, and no RD-1 breach or RD-2 refund is recorded against him here, so no flag_account is set [F18][RD-6]. The safety screen found nothing: the driver's query and the rider's reply are a routing exchange and the driver's statement is a factual account, with no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation in the chat, statement or complaint [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. The record settles every element this ruling needs — complete timestamped chat, segment measurement, a metered fare record and the traffic records — so the evidence is sufficient and no gap is named.

[F9] — a general route authorisation sent before the segment's 09:20 start [F3], which RD-5 makes an exemption for the route chosen to get to the destination. The recorded conditions are consistent with a speed-driven reroute (slow corridor on the optimal route [F12]; free-flowing alternative corridor [F13]; no incident or weather cause [F15][F16]), and no fact shows this loop to be an errand of the driver's own, so no unexempt extra_km remains [RD-5][RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The trip-wide +2.3 km and +10.2 min and the meter totals [F1][F2][F7] are admitted, but RD-2 ties the refund to unexempt off-route segments, not to trip-wide totals, and the only segment is exempt under RD-5 by the rider's pre-segment general authorisation [F9][F3][RD-2][RD-5].

The claim that no RD-3 or RD-4 exemption covers the segment is right but incomplete: RD-4 fails on the absent incident and on the corroborative-only speed band [F12][F15][RD-4], yet RD-5 independently exempts the segment because the rider's own message before it authorised whichever way was faster [F9][F8][F3][RD-5].

The rider's words 'Just take whichever way is faster lah' [F9] are, on the policy's own example, a general route authorisation that RD-5 says covers the route chosen to reach the destination; the record shows no stop or loop serving the driver's own business, so the authorisation reaches this segment [F9][F8][F3][RD-5].

This supports rather than defeats the exemption: RD-4 indeed cannot exempt the segment [F12][F15][RD-4], but the congestion the driver named [F8] and the free-flowing alternative corridor [F13] are what the rider's general authorisation [F9] was exercised on, so the segment is excused under RD-5, not RD-4 [RD-5].

The formula and rate ($30.46 ÷ 21.60 km = $1.4102/km) [F4][F7] are correct, but with the single segment exempt under RD-5 the sum of unexempt extra_km is 0, so 0 × $1.4102 = $0.00 and no refund follows [F3][F9][RD-2][RD-5].

The 0.17 km difference between the billed excess and the segment's extra_km [F3][F4] is corridor noise RD-2 does not restore, but this is immaterial once the segment itself is exempt and the refundable amount is zero [RD-2][RD-5].

RD-6 requires a case established against the driver (RD-2 refund > 0 or an RD-1 breach recorded); no breach is recorded because the segment is exempt, and the trace marks the prior-upheld-route-dispute element ✗ with 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F18][RD-6].

The suggested possibility that the segment was the driver's own business is not borne out by any fact: no stop, no off-route destination and no errand appear in the record, and the only materials tying the segment to a purpose are the congestion exchange and the traffic records [F8][F9][F12][F3][RD-5].

RD-4(a) is not satisfied — no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch [F15] and a speed band alone cannot exempt [F12][RD-4]; the segment is excused by the rider's general authorisation instead [F9][F3][RD-5].

The trip finishing at 35.4 min against a 25.2 min estimate [F2] cannot prove the detour was slower, since the record carries no travel time for the alternative corridor, and it does not displace the rider's pre-segment authorisation of whichever route was faster [F9][F13][RD-5].
